reason: The goal asks for the lane-born stars to enter the crossing, and the returning galaxy's stellar outskirts are where they are approaching.

choice.combine: Stars born in the dark lane
choice.with: Stellar outskirts of the returning galaxy

expectation: The stars will pass through the returning galaxy's outskirts, with their paths affected by gravity.

effect: The lane-born stars crossed the other galaxy without their surfaces colliding, completing the goal and showing how their passage differs from that of their parent gas.
reaction: The contrast between colliding gas and freely passing stars was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Bringing the lane-born stars through the crossing was worthwhile because it connected their formation from colliding gas to their later passage as stars.

leastWorthwhile.text: The chapter offered only one decision, so there was little opportunity to explore alternatives; no passage was particularly confusing or repetitive.

surprise.text: The contrast was striking: the gas collided, but its stellar descendants passed between the other galaxy's stars.

arbitrary.text: The crossing had a clear purpose; no action felt arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. I would be curious to see what happens to the orange star and the smaller sun as the galaxies' story continues.
